## Pan‑African Banking Group – Integration & Market‑Consolidation Blueprint **Scope:**  Acquired banks in **Nigeria (N‑Bank), Kenya (K‑Bank) and Morocco (M‑Bank)** – each with its own core‑banking platform, regulator, language (English, Swahili, Arabic/French) and entrenched management culture. **Goal (12‑month horizon):** Deliver a **single digital‑product suite** (mobile, internet, API‑banking) while preserving **local regulatory compliance, customer continuity and cultural fit** and establishing a **cohesive pan‑African brand** that can scale to future acquisitions. --- ### 1️⃣ Strategic Intent & Success Metrics | Success Area | Target (by Month 12) | How Measured | |--------------|----------------------|--------------| | **Digital‑Product Uniformity** | 90 % of core retail journeys (account opening, payments, loan origination) delivered on a **common UI/UX** platform | Product‑layer coverage KPI (digital‑front‑end) | | **Core‑Banking Consolidation** | 70 % of transaction processing migrated to the **Group Core Engine (GCE)**; legacy systems retired in Nigeria & Kenya (Morocco stays on legacy for 18 mo) | Migration % & System‑Landscape inventory | | **Regulatory Fit‑to‑Fit** | Zero regulatory breach; 100 % of reporting templates aligned to each supervisor (CBN, CBK, Bank Al‑Maghrib) | Compliance audit score | | **Customer‑Experience Continuity** | NPS ≥ 65 in each market; < 2 % drop‑off on key digital services during migration | NPS surveys, churn analytics | | **Brand Cohesion** | 60 % of customers recognise the **Group umbrella brand** alongside local sub‑brand | Brand‑awareness study | | **Management Alignment** | 95 % of senior‑leadership roles filled with **aligned governance charter**; cross‑country leadership council meeting monthly | Org‑chart audit, meeting minutes | | **Cost‑to‑Serve Reduction** | 15 % reduction in total cost‑to‑serve (TCS) vs. FY‑2025 baseline | Finance TCS report | --- ### 2️⃣ Core Integration Principles | Principle | Practical Implication | |-----------|----------------------| | **Modular “Core‑plus‑API” Architecture** | Deploy a **cloud‑native Core Engine (GCE)** that exposes all functions via **open APIs**; legacy cores keep only “back‑office” batch processes during transition. | | **Regulatory‑by‑Design** | Build the **Compliance Service Layer (CSL)** that translates a single internal data model into **regulator‑specific output** (e.g., AML SAR, CBS reporting). | | **Cultural‑Intelligence (CI) First** | Country‑specific CI kits, bilingual change‑management teams, and “Management Shadow‑Boards” that surface local expectations. | | **Brand‑Flexibility** | Adopt a **“Master‑Brand + Local Endorsement”** model – one visual identity with a **local tagline** and a **dual‑language naming convention**. | | **Phased‑Risk‑Based Migration** | Tier‑classify banks (Tier‑A = highest volume/criticality) → **Nigeria (Tier‑A)**, Kenya (Tier‑B), Morocco (Tier‑C). Migration depth follows tier. | | **Digital‑First Collaboration** | A **Supplier‑Collaboration Portal (SCP)** that hosts specifications, test‑cases, regulatory artefacts, translation glossaries and real‑time issue tracking. | | **Continuous‑Improvement Loop** | Monthly “Integration Health‑Check” that captures defect, delay, or cultural friction; feed directly into a **Kaizen backlog**. | --- ### 3️⃣ Governance Structure ``` PAN‑AFRICA GROUP BOARD | ------------------------------------------------- | | | | INTEGRATION REGULATORY BRAND & MARKETING TECHNOLOGY OFFICE (IO) COMPLIANCE & COMMUNICATION COE | | | | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | | | | | NIGERIA KENYA MOROCCO LEGAL CI/HR DIGITAL CORE DATA LLOs LLOs LLOs (Reg) (CX) (Enable) ENGINE MGMT ``` * **Integration Office (IO)** – Executive sponsor (Chief Integration Officer) + three **Local Lead Officers (LLOs)** (one per country). * **Regulatory Compliance Hub** – Central team of 4 legal/compliance officers with one **Regulatory Liaison** per jurisdiction. * **Brand & Communication** – Central Brand Manager + local **Market‑Brand Champions** (language‑aware). * **Technology COE** – Core Engine architects, API‑gatekeepers, data‑governance lead, and **Migration Squad** (DevOps, QA, Business‑Analyst). All decisions pass through a **Monthly Integration Steering Committee** (IO + Reg‑Hub + Brand + Tech COE). **RACI matrix** attached in Annex A. --- ### 4️⃣ Phase‑Gate Integration Roadmap | Phase | Duration | Core Objective | Owner(s) | Key Deliverables | |-------|----------|----------------|----------|------------------| | **0️⃣ Discovery & Baseline** | 4 wks | • Map legacy core‑banking landscapes (Finacle, Temenos, T24).

• Weekly **Customer‑Experience Pulse** (NPS, CSAT) – feed to product‑owner backlog.

• **30‑day Audit Report**.
• **Maturity Upgrade Decision** (Tier‑move). | > **Gate Review** – Advance to next phase only after documented sign‑off from **IO, Reg‑Hub, Brand & Tech COE** (quality, compliance, brand‑fit). --- ### 5️⃣ Technology Migration Sequencing (Detail) | Step | Action | Tools / Platforms | Owner | |------|--------|-------------------|-------| | **5.1 Data‑Model Harmonisation** | Build **Unified Business Ontology (UBO)** (customer, account, transaction).
Map each legacy data element → UBO. | *Informatica MDM*, *Collibra* (data‑catalog) | Data‑Gov Lead | | **5.2 API‑Facade Layer** | For each legacy core, expose **REST/SOAP adapters** that translate to UBO calls.
Deploy **API‑Gateway** (Kong/Apigee) with **policy‑based routing** (country‑specific). | *Kong*, *AWS API Gateway* | Platform Engineer | | **5.3 Core‑Engine Deployment** | **GCE** (e.g., *Finacle Cloud* or *Temenos Transact* SaaS) provisioned in **AWS Africa (Cape Town) & Azure (UAE) for redundancy**.

Batch‑reconcile daily balances – automated exception alerts. | *Confluent Kafka*, *DBSync* | Ops Lead | | **5.5 Cut‑Over Strategy** | **Blue‑Green Switch** – DNS & routing change at 02:00 local time, with a 2‑hour rollback window. | *Route 53*, *Azure Traffic Manager* | Release Manager | | **5.6 Post‑Cut‑Over Validation** | Run **End‑to‑End Functional Tests** (Cypress), **Performance Load** (JMeter – 200 TPS), **Security Pen‑Test** (OWASP ZAP). | *Cypress*, *JMeter*, *ZAP* | QA Lead | | **5.7 Legacy De‑commission** | After 60 days of stable operation, **archive** legacy DB → **Cold‑storage** (S3 Glacier). | *AWS S3 Glacier* | Data‑Retention Officer | --- ### 6️⃣ Brand Decision Framework | Dimension | Option | Rationale | Implementation | |-----------|--------|-----------|----------------| | **Master‑Brand vs. Local Brands** | **Master‑Brand “AfriBank”** with **Local Endorsement** (“AfriBank Nigeria”) | Provides pan‑African identity for digital products, leverages economies of scale in marketing, yet respects local brand equity (e.g., “M‑Bank” legacy trust). | • Joint‑branding rollout over 6 months.
• Co‑branded advertising (TV, radio, digital) with **local language tagline**. | | **Logo & Visual System** | Single logo, **colour palette** derived from *Pan‑African* palette; *local icon* added per market (e.g., baobab for Nigeria, acacia for Kenya, Atlas for Morocco). | Visual cohesion, easy to recognise across borders; local icon conveys cultural relevance. | • Brand Asset Management System (Bynder). | | **Digital Front‑End UI** | **Unified UI‑kit** (React‑Native for mobile, Angular for web) with **language packs** (EN, SW, AR, FR). | Uniform product experience, faster release cycles. | • Localization engine (i18next) + **translation memory** for technical terms. | | **Marketing Messaging** | Core value proposition – **“Secure, Seamless, Africa‑wide Banking”**; local pillars – *financial inclusion* (Kenya), *SME growth* (Nigeria), *Islamic‑finance compliance* (Morocco). | Aligns with regulator priorities and customer expectations. | • Market‑specific creative briefs, 3‑month campaign calendar. | --- ### 7️⃣ Management Alignment – People & Culture | Action | Execution Steps | Owner | |--------|-----------------|-------| | **Leadership Council (RLC)** | • 3 core members (CEO‑group, Country‑CEO, COO‑group).

bars indicate overlapping workstreams.) --- ### 12️⃣ Resource & Budget Summary (Year 1) | Function | FTE (Headcount) | Key Roles | Estimated Cost (US$) | |----------|-----------------|-----------|----------------------| | **Integration Office** | 5 | CIO, 3 LLOs, Integration PM | 1.2 M | | **Regulatory & Compliance** | 4 | Reg‑Legal Lead, 3 Reg‑Liaisons | 0.9 M | | **Technology COE** | 12 | Core Engine Architects, API Designers, Cloud Ops, QA, Data‑Gov | 2.4 M | | **Brand & Communications** | 3 | Brand Manager, Creative Lead, Localization Specialist | 0.6 M | | **CI & HR** | 2 | CI Trainer, Change‑Management Lead | 0.4 M | | **External Services** | – | Cloud infra (AWS/Azure), SaaS licences (Ariba, Confluence, Bynder), RegTech vendor | 0.7 M | | **Contingency (10 %)** | – | – | 0.6 M | | **Total** | **≈ 28 FTE** | – | **≈ US $6.8 M** | *(Capital expenditure for hardware, data‑center upgrades excluded – already covered by existing Group IT budget.)* --- ### 13️⃣ Quick‑Start Checklist (First 30 Days) | ✅ | Immediate Action | |---|-------------------| | 1 | **Appoint LLOs** for Nigeria, Kenya, Morocco; give them authority on daily escalations. | | 2 | **Create Central Integration Office** (IO) – secure workspace, communication channels (Teams, SCP). | | 3 | **Run Baseline Surveys** – Core‑Landscape, Regulatory Matrix, Cultural‑Fit (target 5‑day turnaround). | | 4 | **Sign off “Master‑Brand” name** with legal & marketing; upload brand kit to Bynder. | | 5 | **Provision GCE sandbox** on AWS – run first “Hello‑World” transaction to validate API‑Facade. | | 6 | **Configure RegTech adapters** for CBN, CBK, Bank Al‑Maghrib (sample files). | | 7 | **Launch CI Bootcamp** (online) for all senior leaders – complete within 2 weeks. | | 8 | **Set up KPI Dashboard** (Power BI) pulling data from SCP, cloud logs, finance system. | | 9 | **Schedule first Migration Run‑Book** meeting (Nigeria) – define cut‑over window. | | 10| **Publish Customer FAQ** (multilingual) on upcoming digital product changes. | --- ## Closing Narrative The **key to success** lies in treating each market **as a distinct ecosystem** while **leveraging a single, modern digital backbone**. By: 1. **Standardising the data and service layer** (GCE + Compliance Service Layer) – you gain speed, scalability, and a single point for security‑by‑design. 2. **Embedding regulatory‑by‑design adapters** – you avoid costly re‑work and keep every supervisor satisfied. 3. **Adopting a “Master‑Brand + Local Endorsement”** model – you build a continent‑wide identity that still resonates with the trust built by each legacy bank. 4. **Putting cultural‑intelligence and leadership alignment at the centre** – you minimise talent churn and ensure decisions are made with local nuance. The phased, risk‑based migration schedule (Nigeria → Kenya → Morocco) respects the **different criticalities** of each core system while delivering **early wins** (digital product unification) that can be showcased to regulators and customers alike. The governance framework, KPI‑driven scorecard and continuous‑improvement loop guarantee that any deviation is spotted early, corrected quickly, and fed back into the playbook for the next market. **Result:** By the end of the first year the Group will operate a **single, secure digital banking platform**, present a **cohesive pan‑African brand**, and maintain **full regulatory compliance**—setting the foundation for further expansion across the continent.
